title: Forecast allocation versus physical realization policy contrast

dependency_gate.implementation_rule: No DUMMY-15B model or tests before DUMMY-15 qualification and baseline rebinding.

purpose: Reproduce the original conflict where management allocation sees enough predicted surface-water capacity, but later shared-state hydrology reduces the physically realizable managed withdrawal.

stage_contract.forecast_capacity: M_pred is an explicit allocation-stage capacity estimate; first canonical forecast ignores surface-groundwater exchange and uses A_s*(h_s0-hmin).
stage_contract.allocation: Split min(R_root+R_ext,M_pred) lexicographically by the declared managed priority. Record allocated_root and allocated_ext.
stage_contract.realization: Submit the allocated total to the qualified shared-state physical management oracle to obtain the exact total physically supplied M_actual and physical exchange V.
stage_contract.realization_split: Evaluate at least two explicit supplied-flow policies against the same allocated vector and same M_actual: (A) priority-preserving curtailment oracle; (B) proportional aggregate-reduction oracle with rho=M_actual/sum(allocated), supplied_i=rho*allocated_i. Policy B is a structural analogue of documented aggregate UserDemand reduction, not an exact reproduction of Ribasim's smooth phi functions.
stage_contract.commit: Only supplied flows and physical exchange enter the water ledger and accepted states. Allocated-but-unsupplied water is diagnostic only.

invariants: sum supplied_i equals the exact coupled realized managed total for the allocated request
allocated-but-unsupplied volumes do not enter any physical storage balance
physical exchange V is not clipped to protect allocation
root state changes by supplied root irrigation, not allocated root irrigation
combined three-store storage change equals minus supplied external demand when root external forcing is zero

forecast.interpretation: surface-only storage above hmin appears sufficient for both managed claims

underallocation_control.purpose: Show that actual physical capacity may exceed the allocated total; realization must not create unallocated managed delivery.

hypotheses: The canonical surface-only forecast allocates the full 60 m3, but exact shared-state realization supplies only 32 m3 because the mandatory physical exchange is 28 m3 at the accepted endpoint.
Both realization policies preserve 0 <= supplied_i <= allocated_i <= demand_i and sum supplied_i=M_actual.

Priority-preserving curtailment and proportional aggregate reduction can produce different supplied splits, root memory and represented-system loss despite identical allocation, identical M_actual, identical V and identical surface/groundwater endpoint.

Under full canonical allocation, priority-preserving root-first gives supplied_root=32 and supplied_external=0, while proportional reduction gives supplied_root=21.3333333333 and supplied_external=10.6666666667.
Allocated-but-unsupplied water never appears in any physical storage balance under either policy.
When forecast allocation is below what the physical system can realize, supplied flow cannot exceed allocated flow under either policy.

Changing forecast capacity can change allocation and thereby the physical attempted managed total; it cannot change the rule that physical exchange is solved from the actually attempted/supplied coupling problem.
A forecast error is a management-information error, not a license to alter the physical exchange law.
DUMMY-15B does not decide which realization policy production coupling should use; it creates exact contrasting oracles for later pinned Ribasim evidence.

public_authority_binding.note: Current public documentation distinguishes demand, allocated and supplied. DUMMY-15B remains a one-Basin analytical realization oracle and does not claim exact Ribasim physical-layer curtailment semantics.
public_authority_binding.documented_physical_behavior: Current UserDemand abstraction equals smooth low-storage and min-level reduction factors times the sum of allocated flows (capped by current demand), so actual supplied abstraction can be lower than allocated abstraction.
public_authority_binding.policy_consequence: This documentation invalidates any unqualified claim that current Ribasim necessarily preserves demand priority during physical curtailment after allocation.

forbidden: no claim that either analytical realization policy exactly reproduces current Ribasim across arbitrary networks/nodes
no claim that priority-preserving curtailment is current Ribasim supplied-flow behavior without executable evidence
no network routing or allocation fairness in DUMMY-15B
no production SWAP irrigation authority claim
preregistration_revision_note: Revised before any DUMMY-15B implementation after checking current Ribasim UserDemand/allocation documentation. Current UserDemand physical abstraction applies smooth reduction factors to the allocated amount; this is not inherently equivalent to lower-priority-first curtailment. DUMMY-15B therefore compares realization policies instead of assuming priority-preserving realization is current Ribasim behavior.

priority_preserving.purpose: Management-intent oracle: retain the declared demand priority during physical curtailment.
priority_preserving.rule: Walk the allocation vector in priority order; supplied_i=min(allocated_i, remaining_actual_capacity).

proportional_aggregate_reduction.purpose: Structural reference for a physical layer that reduces already-allocated abstractions with a common source-state factor.
proportional_aggregate_reduction.ribasim_boundary: Current UserDemand documentation multiplies allocated abstraction by smooth low-storage and min-level reduction factors. DUMMY-15B uses rho only to isolate split semantics; it does not reproduce the exact phi functions or assert identical scaling across arbitrary distinct real nodes.
